correctness.rationale: The survival function is continuous, positive, and defines an absolutely continuous probability law. Exact integration gives \(m_X(x)=1+2e^{x-1}\) for \(0<x<1\) and \(m_X(x)=3\) for \(x>1\); the derivative of \(m_X(x)/x\) is strictly negative on both pieces and the quotient is continuous at \(x=1\). With \(T=1+3\log(5/4)\), the truncated survival is \(S_Y(x)=(S_X(x)-S_X(T))/(1-S_X(T))\), the left hazard limit at \(x=1\) equals \(5\), and \(m_Y(1)=3-12\log(5/4)\). Differentiating the survival integral gives \(\lim_{x\uparrow1}\ell_Y'(x)=11-48\log(5/4)>1/4\), certified by the exact alternating-series bound \(\log(5/4)<43/192\). The standalone checker reproduces the rational certificate and high-precision diagnostics; the analytic proof covers all required positive ages and a genuine open interval of violation.

broader_coverage.reasoning: IGFR implies DGMRL, but the existing right-truncation closure theorem only covers IGFR sources. The exhibited piecewise exponential lifetime is not IGFR because its generalized hazard drops from \(1\) to \(1/3\) at the switch; thus IGFR preservation neither implies nor conflicts with this nonclosure example. Literature on ordinary MRL or right censoring addresses different properties or operations.

value.rationale: Right-truncation closure of the DGMRL class is explicitly posed as unresolved by primary research, and determines whether a useful stochastic-demand and reliability aging condition survives information updates imposing finite ceilings. The explicit two-rate, connected-support, absolutely continuous counterexample settles this natural binary question, exposes the distinction from established IGFR preservation, and has a strict exact one-sided derivative margin. The result is not merely a numerical observation or a reformulation of a textbook derivative identity.
